svg.title: ASAR Control Studio — Architecture Overview
svg.desc: Architecture diagram showing ASAR as a web application. Users configure ESP32 boards and choose between two mobile/remote access paths: Path A integrates Blynk Cloud for remote access via the Blynk mobile app; Path B uses Mobile App Studio to generate a custom Android APK whose widget layout is synced from ASAR.
svg.text: ASAR Control Studio — Architecture Overview
Web-first application: configure ESP32, then choose remote/mobile access via Blynk Cloud (Path A) or a generated Android APK (Path B)
Stack: React + Vite + TypeScript · Capacitor for Android packaging · ESP32 Arduino firmware generated from config
ASAR Web Application
Runs in any browser · No native install · React + Vite + TypeScript
Board Config Panel
Board name, chip family, Wi-Fi SSID/password, hostname, server port, baud rate
OTA · mDNS · logging · API base URL · poll interval
enableBlynk · blynkTemplateId · blynkAuthToken · blynkServer:Port · heartbeatMs
Pins: id, GPIO number, label, mode (INPUT/OUTPUT/PWM/ANALOG), blynkVPin
Persisted to localStorage on every change · restored on page reload
Sketch Panel — Arduino Code Generator
generateSketch(config) → .ino text preview in the UI
getSketchFileName(config) → project-name.ino
Download: Blob → object URL → anchor.click() → .ino file to disk
Includes Wi-Fi, HTTP routes, OTA, mDNS, pins, optional Blynk client
Mobile App Studio
Visual widget dashboard builder (drag-and-drop, reorder)
Widget kinds: Toggle · Push Button · Slider · Status Card · Logs Feed
Each widget assigned to a GPIO pin, min/max values, action value
Set app name, package ID, and target API base URL
Exports widget config as package/mobile-app/package-info.json
Scripts: package:mobile copies dist → package/mobile-app/www for APK build
Device Panels — Live Control
Polls GET /api/status every pollIntervalMs → online, IP, RSSI, freeHeap, uptime, pins[]
Polls GET /api/logs → log entries [{level, message, createdAt}]
Sends POST /api/pins/:pin with plain-text value (0, 1, or 0–255 for PWM)
Marks device offline on fetch failure; stores error in in-memory logs
Connection states: idle → probing → online | offline
localStorage (Persistence)
Key: "asar-control-studio" → full BoardConfig JSON
Key: "asar-mobile-app-studio:v1" → MobileStudioConfig JSON
lib/storage.ts: loadConfig(default) / saveConfig(config)
Why Web-First?
· No install required — runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox on any OS
· Configuration always synced across sessions via localStorage
· Direct HTTP access to ESP32 on the same LAN (no backend needed)
· Use ASAR as the single source of truth for both firmware and mobile UI
· npm run dev: localhost dev server
· npm run build: static assets → deploy to any web host or serve locally
· Capacitor wraps the built assets into an APK for offline/sideloaded use
ESP32 Firmware Layer
Arduino target · flashed via Arduino IDE or OTA · serves HTTP + optional Blynk
Generated Arduino Sketch (.ino)
Wi-Fi connect (SSID + password from config)
HTTP server on configured port
GET /api/status, GET /api/logs, POST /api/pins/:pin
Optional: OTA update endpoint · mDNS announce · serial logging
Optional: Blynk client — BLYNK_TEMPLATE_ID, BLYNK_AUTH_TOKEN
Virtual pins V0–V255 mapped to PinDefinition.blynkVPin
Pin setup/loop blocks derived from pins[] in BoardConfig
▼ User flashes via Arduino IDE / OTA / esptool
ESP32 — Running Firmware
HTTP API (Local LAN)
GET /api/status
→ {online, ip, rssi, freeHeap, uptimeMs, board, pins[]}
GET /api/logs
→ [{level, message, createdAt}]
POST /api/pins/:pin body: "0" | "1" | "0-255"
→ 200 OK · writes GPIO / PWM channel
Polled by ASAR Device Panels every pollIntervalMs
Available on LAN · accessible by Android APK on same network
esp32.local (mDNS) or direct IP address
Blynk Client (enableBlynk = true)
Persistent TCP/TLS connection to blynk.cloud:443
Sends heartbeat every blynkHeartbeatMs
BLYNK_TEMPLATE_ID + BLYNK_AUTH_TOKEN embedded at sketch gen
Virtual pin mapping: V{pin.blynkVPin} ↔ GPIO {pin.pin}
BLYNK_WRITE(Vn) handler: sets GPIO value on command from cloud
Blynk.virtualWrite(Vn, value): pushes live sensor/pin state up
Works over any network — ESP32 reaches blynk.cloud regardless
of LAN topology (phone can be on 4G, ESP32 on home Wi-Fi)
Both HTTP API and Blynk client run simultaneously when enabled
Configured in BoardConfigPanel under "Blynk Integration" section
Board config fields: blynkTemplateId, blynkTemplateName,
blynkAuthToken, blynkServer, blynkPort, blynkHeartbeatMs
Pin State
Physical GPIO/PWM written on POST /api/pins/:pin or Blynk BLYNK_WRITE
Pin values broadcast in /api/status response and Blynk virtual writes
Path A — Blynk Remote Access
Remote control over the internet · no APK build needed · install Blynk App from store
REMOTE
Blynk Cloud (blynk.cloud)
Managed cloud broker — stores real-time virtual pin state
Routes commands bidirectionally between ESP32 and Blynk mobile app
Transport: persistent TCP over TLS (port 443, configurable)
Device identified by BLYNK_TEMPLATE_ID + BLYNK_AUTH_TOKEN
Free tier available · no self-hosted server needed
Register at blynk.cloud → copy Template ID + Auth Token → paste into ASAR
Blynk Mobile App (iOS / Android)
Install from Apple App Store or Google Play Store — no APK build needed
Dashboard editor: drag-and-drop Button, Slider, Gauge, Value Display widgets
Each widget mapped to a Virtual Pin (V0–V255)
Widget value ↔ ESP32 GPIO value via cloud relay in real time
Works over any network — 4G, 5G, home Wi-Fi, mobile hotspot
Device does not need a public IP — ESP32 reaches out to blynk.cloud
Multiple devices and apps supported under one template
Blynk V-pin assignments are configured per pin inside ASAR BoardConfigPanel
PinDefinition.blynkVPin → V{n} in generated sketch and Blynk dashboard
Workflow: configure in ASAR → download sketch → flash ESP32 → open Blynk App
ASAR can still poll ESP32 HTTP API in parallel while Blynk is active
Use case: monitor sensors remotely, toggle outputs from anywhere in the world
Path B — Custom Android APK
Self-hosted mobile app · widget layout synced from ASAR Mobile App Studio · connects to ESP32 via HTTP
LOCAL/LAN
APK Package (Capacitor / Cordova)
Widget layout and app metadata synced from Mobile App Studio config
Build step: npm run build:web copies dist/ into package/mobile-app/www/
script: scripts/package-mobile.mjs + scripts/quick-package-and-dev.mjs
Capacitor config: capacitor.config.ts → android/ folder (Gradle project)
Build APK: cd android → gradlew assembleDebug or assembleRelease
quick-build-package-apk.ps1 / quick-build-package-apk.bat automate this
Android Application (Sideloaded / Play Store)
Connects to ESP32 HTTP API (/api/status, /api/logs, /api/pins/:pin)
Requires ESP32 reachable over local Wi-Fi network or port-forwarded
targetApiBaseUrl set in Mobile App Studio (e.g. http://192.168.x.x or http://esp32.local)
Widget dashboard mirrors the layout designed in ASAR Mobile App Studio
Fully offline-capable once installed — no cloud service required
Use case: dedicated on-site tablet or phone permanently paired to ESP32
Update app: rebuild APK in ASAR pipeline, reinstall on device
packageId set in Mobile App Studio (e.g. com.asar.myproject)
Advantage over Blynk APK: fully custom brand, no third-party cloud dependency

Legend
ASAR Web App (React + Vite)
ESP32 Firmware (Arduino .ino)
Path A — Blynk Cloud (remote, any network)
Path B — Custom Android APK (local LAN, no cloud)
HTTP poll / command (ASAR ↔ ESP32)
Sketch generation / download
Blynk TLS heartbeat + V-pin sync
Config sync → APK build pipeline
Android APK → ESP32 HTTP API (same LAN)
Telemetry response (ESP32 → ASAR)

Source files: src/App.tsx · src/types.ts · src/components/BoardConfigPanel.tsx · src/components/MobileAppStudio.tsx · src/components/SketchPanel.tsx · src/components/DevicePanels.tsx · src/lib/sketch.ts · src/lib/storage.ts · capacitor.config.ts · scripts/package-mobile.mjs
Architecture decision: ASAR is a web-first application. Blynk (Path A) enables zero-build remote access. Custom APK (Path B) provides offline, brandable mobile control without cloud dependency.
